correctness.rationale: For every 0<alpha,beta<1 and t>0, exact stable and inverse-stable Mellin transforms give the claimed hyperbolic-sine ratio. Its explicit Levy density is globally positive by strict convexity of y -> 1/(exp(x exp(-y))-1), with valid small- and large-x integrability. Levy-Khintchine provides an independent centered symmetric infinitely divisible factor; characteristic function uniqueness and conditional Jensen prove strict log convex order. The log variance formula follows by a second derivative. The proof is analytical; finite diagnostics of 750 checks are supplemental.

originality.rationale: The motivating paper defines the two clock orders but does not compare them. Previous mixed-product/Mellin work computes densities, and Simon compares distinct stability indices: none supplies the crucial strict positivity of the four-term Levy kernel or the independent noise factor for reversed compositions. Literature searches found no logically dominating result. A residual historical priority risk is acknowledged.
residual_risks: An unlocated earlier stochastic-order, logistic-factorization or Lévy-kernel theorem may imply the same claim; search absence is not a priority certificate.
The cited time-change paper assumes finite moments for several results; this theorem instead independently treats infinite-mean positive stable clocks.
No independent peer assessment has been performed.

value.rationale: The two natural subordination orderings exhibit the same homogeneity and mean log-clock, yet their dispersions differ for all parameters. The independent symmetric ID factor proves dominance for all convex tests rather than one routine variance calculation. An explicit Levy density gives a structural comparison of clock compositions of potential use in selecting models of random-time heterogeneity, with accurate one-time-scope limitations.
